title: Why does every keyboard have two tiny bumps?
hook: Run your finger over F and J. Those two little bumps were invented by one person, and they were patented.

title: Why do pen caps have a hole in the top?
hook: That tiny hole in your pen cap isn't for the ink. It's there to save your life.

title: Why do airplane windows have a tiny hole?
hook: Look closely at a plane window. There's a hole the size of a pin, and the plane needs it.

title: Why do jeans have tiny metal rivets?
hook: Those little copper dots on your jeans were a patent, and a tailor's trick that made one company famous.

title: Why are keyboards not in ABC order?
hook: Your keyboard is scrambled on purpose, and the reason is a 150-year-old machine.

title: Why is red always on top of a traffic light?
hook: Every traffic light in the world puts red on top. It isn't random.

title: Why does a bottle cap have exactly 21 teeth?
hook: Count the ridges on a glass-bottle cap. There are almost always 21, and an inventor decided that.

title: Why does your phone have a tiny hole next to the camera?
hook: That pinhole on the back of your phone isn't a camera. It's listening.

title: Why is the bottom of a soda can curved inward?
hook: Flip a soda can over. That dome isn't decoration. Without it the can could burst.

title: Velcro was invented because of a dog walk
hook: A man came home from a walk covered in sticky seeds, and that annoying moment became Velcro.

title: The sticky note was a failed glue
hook: The glue on sticky notes was a failure. It was too weak. That's exactly why it works.

title: Why does your microwave door have a metal mesh?
hook: Look through your microwave door. That grid of tiny holes is the only thing between you and the waves.

title: How does GPS know where you are?
hook: Your phone finds you using clocks in space, and without Einstein they'd be wrong by kilometres every day.

title: Why is the barcode made of stripes?
hook: The barcode was first drawn with fingers in beach sand, from Morse code.

title: Why do zippers never fall apart?
hook: A zipper locks hundreds of tiny teeth in a second. It took 20 years of failures to get it right.

title: Why do ships and planes use 'Mayday'?
hook: Mayday isn't English. It comes from a French phrase picked in 1923.

title: Why do car tyres have grooves?
hook: A smooth tyre grips better on a dry road. So why are your tyres full of grooves?

title: Why are pencils yellow?
hook: Almost every pencil is yellow, and it started as a boast about China.

title: Who stole an hour of your sleep? The clock change
hook: This weekend millions of clocks jump back an hour, because of an idea from a bug collector.

title: Why are blue fireworks the hardest to make?
hook: Red, green, gold are easy. Blue fireworks are so hard that chemists still compete to make them.

title: Scientists predicted the end of the world for Friday 13 November 2026
hook: In 1960, a real science journal printed a paper that named the day humanity's population would hit infinity: Friday, 13 November 2026.

title: Japan just launched a robot to steal dirt from a moon of Mars
hook: Japan has launched a probe to grab soil from Phobos, a moon of Mars, and bring it home. No one has ever done that.

title: This robot has driven farther than any vehicle on another world
hook: A car on Mars has now driven 45 kilometres, and it did almost all of it by itself.

title: A space telescope built to last 2 years worked for 21. Now it's falling
hook: NASA built Swift to last two years. It worked for twenty-one, and now it's falling back to Earth.

title: Dying coral came back to life just by touching a friend
hook: Scientists put a bleached, dying coral next to a healthy one. Seven weeks later it was fully alive again.

title: Why your body only uses left-handed molecules
hook: Your hands are mirror images. So are many molecules, but life uses only one hand. That mystery just won a Nobel Prize.

title: Trillions of ghost particles are passing through you right now
hook: Right now, trillions of tiny particles are flying straight through your body. A telescope made of Antarctic ice just won a Nobel for catching them.

title: These tiny snakes roll like wheels
hook: Scientists filmed tiny snakes that curl into a hoop and roll, four times faster than they can slither.

title: MIT built a robot powered by real muscle, controlled by light
hook: This swimming robot has living muscle on its fins, and you steer it by shining a light.

title: Astronomers found the first green star
hook: Stars are red, yellow, white or blue, but never green. Until now.
